title: What is compound interest? — Investor.gov, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Office of Investor Education and Advocacy)

transcription: Article text only (the audience 'Main navigation' menu, site header and footer, Related/Featured content cards and the Spanish-language toggle removed). The H1 kept as the '# ' title line; 'Rule of 72' and 'Suggested student activities' headings kept as plain lines. Bullets flattened one per line with • markers; the nested pizza questions kept at the same level with their bracketed answer keys as printed ('[The correct answer is $730.]'). The page's missing period after 'almost $340' kept as served. Straight and curly quotes mixed as printed. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: compound interest for students — the $100-at-5% worked example ($105 after year one, $110.25 after year two including $0.25 interest-on-interest, more than $162 after 10 years, almost $340 after 25), the Rule of 72 stated as a division (72 divided by 9 equals 8 years to double), and the pizza-savings exercises with answer key ($2 x 365 = $730 a year; $931.69 after five years at 5%; $3,155.02 after 30). Fits the compound-interest formula explorer, quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on every worked answer, and Rule-of-72 arithmetic.
